summary: Provides a model and requirements for message tracking, the ability to learn the path a message has taken through a messaging system and its current status. It was written to answer a common customer question about enterprise messaging systems.

eli5.summary: Delivery tracking for email, such as a package tracker that tells you each stop along the way. This document explains how that should work.

questions: how can i track an email message
subtitle: Tracking email messages through the mail system

tldr.problem: Email users want to know where a message is in the mail system and whether it has been delivered, but there is no standardized way to track messages across different mail systems.
tldr.mechanism: The document provides a model for message tracking that builds on existing protocols like DSN (Delivery Status Notification) and MDN (Message Disposition Notification), along with requirements for tracking servers and clients to query message status.
tldr.outcome: This model enables developers to build message tracking applications that work across multiple email systems and domains, giving users package-delivery-like visibility into their messages.

facts.label: Key requirement
facts.value: Only message originator or delegate can track

today: RFC 3888 is an Informational RFC that defines the model and requirements for message tracking. While it has not been obsoleted, the actual tracking implementations described in related RFCs like RFC 3885, RFC 3886, and RFC 3887 provide the specific protocols to realize this model.

sections.title: The Problem
sections.content: RFC 3888 addresses a common request from email system users: the ability to track where a message is in the mail system and its current delivery status. The document compares this to package delivery tracking, where a customer can determine if a package has been delivered and, if not, where it currently is. Message tracking extends this capability to the Internet email infrastructure, allowing users to quickly locate a message and determine its current status as it travels through one or more mail systems.
sections.eli5: Just like you can track a package through a delivery company to see where it is, you should be able to track an email message to know if it has arrived.

sections.title: Key Entities in Message Tracking
sections.content:
The tracking model involves several entities. Mail User Agents (MUA) are the programs used to compose and read email. Mail Submission Agents (MSA) accept messages from users and inject them into the network. Message Transfer Agents (MTA) move messages toward their destination, either as intermediate MTAs or final MTAs. Local Delivery Agents (LDA) deliver messages to the local message store. Tracking User Agents (TUA) request tracking information, while Tracking Servers provide that information.

The model also uses Delivery Status Notifications (DSN) to report when a message succeeds or fails at each step, and Message Disposition Notifications (MDN) to report whether a user has read a message.
sections.eli5: Different programs handle email at different stages: one writes it, one sends it out, others pass it along, one delivers it, and special services track it and report back.

sections.title: Tracking Models and Requirements
sections.content:
Message tracking can use either a passive or active enabling model. Passive enabling assumes tracking is on by default with no special setup needed. Active enabling requires the Mail User Agent and Mail Submission Agent to exchange information to enable tracking. Similarly, tracking information can be retrieved passively (automatically sent back) or actively (queried when needed).

When a tracking user agent queries a tracking server for information, the tracking server can either contact the next server in the chain to get complete status (server chaining) or return the address of the next server and let the client query it (server referrals).

The RFC requires that tracking solutions must scale to the Internet, be easy to deploy, reuse existing technology where possible, restrict tracking to the message originator or a delegate, and uniquely identify messages.
sections.eli5: Tracking can be set up automatically or when you ask for it. When you want to know where your email is, the system can either look it up itself or tell you who to ask.

sections.title: Security and Privacy
sections.content:
Message tracking introduces security concerns that must be addressed. One key issue is authentication: a Tracking User Agent must prove that it is permitted to request tracking information about a message. The RFC proposes a security model using one-way hashing, where the originator calculates a hash of the message ID, a timestamp, and a per-user secret, then calculates a second hash of that hash. The first hash is retained by the originator and the second is included in the message. Later, when requesting tracking information, the originator submits the first hash, allowing the tracking server to verify the request is authentic.

Other security considerations include protection against snooping and replay attacks, reliance on TLS encryption, protection against man-in-the-middle attacks, and prevention of denial-of-service attacks. If the originator delegates tracking requests to a third party, additional risks arise during transmission of the authentication token.
sections.eli5: Only the person who sent the email should be able to track it. The system uses secret codes to prove who is asking for tracking information.

sections.title: Interaction with Other Mechanisms
sections.content:
Message tracking information can work together with Delivery Status Notifications (DSN) and Message Disposition Notifications (MDN). DSN is used to report the success or failure of message delivery at each stage, while MDN reports whether a recipient has read the message. Message tracking provides additional information about the path the message took and its current location at intermediate systems. A tracking user agent could use all three information sources to provide users with a comprehensive view of message status.

The RFC notes that the tracking information format should be similar to the formats already used by DSN and MDN for consistency across different tracking solutions.
sections.eli5: Email already has systems to report success or failure and to show if someone read it. Tracking adds information about where the email is right now.
